o1.biggest_strength: A sharp single recommendation aimed at the Essentials 8+ leak. The per-1,000-customer churn scenarios are correct, the stop rules are clean, and the invite email is in our voice, with the customer's own price difference shown.
o1.biggest_mistake: It talks itself out of the yearly-billing push with a shaky payback argument and ignores the 0.9% vs 4.0% churn gap. That leaves the cheapest fast win off the table, and the yearly default on the pricing page is never fixed.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add an honest yearly nudge alongside Agency, either an in-app offer or a yearly default on the page. Show a total-business net figure with the Team downgrade assumption built in, not only per-1,000 switchers.

o2.biggest_strength: The whole-business view: the Essentials 8+ share of churned revenue, base and downside cases with Team downgrades netted out, and the break-even downgrade rate. It also tests downgrade risk directly on Team customers and offers yearly at the switch.
o2.biggest_mistake: The customer message is a little softer and less concrete than it could be: it shows no price difference and has a slightly generic opening. The day-one net of +$2.7k is thin, and the plan doesn't flag clearly enough that most of the gain depends on an unproven churn drop.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Show each customer the exact difference in the email. Add a yearly default on the pricing page as a parallel quick test. State plainly that new prices only reach new customers, so the two-quarter gain rests on retention.

reason: Both make the same right call. The second one gives me the whole-business numbers including Team downgrades, tests that risk directly, and keeps the yearly-billing win in play, so I'd take it to the board.
